title: A Taylor step for g(h)
caption: g(h)/g₀ = (1 + h/R)⁻² (curve) is replaced by its first Taylor step 1 − 2h/R (dashed line), whose gradient −2 matches the curve at h = 0. At h = 10 km, h/R = 0.0016 and g has fallen by only 0.3%, where line and curve are indistinguishable. Far above the surface (right of the graph) they part company.
alt: Graph of g over g0 against h over R: a curve (1 + h/R)^-2 and its tangent line 1 − 2h/R, which agree near zero and separate as h/R grows.
description: Horizontal axis: h/R, the height as a fraction of the Earth's radius; vertical axis: g/g₀.
The curve is g/g₀ = (1 + h/R)⁻². The dashed line is 1 − 2h/R, the first-order Taylor series about h = 0.
Near the surface the two are indistinguishable. At h = 10 km, h/R = 0.0016 and g/g₀ = 0.9969: a 0.3% fall.
At h/R = 0.3 the line has dropped to 0.4 but the true value is 0.59: the step is only valid for small h/R.

checks.name: the gradient of g/g₀ at h = 0 is −2 (the Taylor coefficient)
at h = 10 km, the Taylor step gives 1 − 2h/R = 0.997 (0.3% lower)
the straight line gives 0.4 at h/R = 0.3 (the step fails there)
